# Hook Generator AI: 50 Scroll-Stopping Video Hooks for 5 Creator Niches

If you searched "hook generator ai", you probably want opening lines for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts that you can use today. You don't need a lecture on attention spans. This page gives you 50 ready-to-film hooks across five creator niches. Each one has three parts:

- **Spoken line:** what you say in the first three seconds, kept to about 12 words.
- **On-screen text:** the overlay viewers read with the sound off.
- **Hook type:** curiosity, contrarian, stakes, result, or callout. Mixing types lets you A/B test instead of guessing.

Every example uses the Hook Lab method: a clear positioning angle, a specific topic, varied hook types, and no made-up numbers. Where a hook needs a figure only you have, you'll see `[ADD: your number]`. Replace it with your real result or drop the hook.

---

## How to Choose and Test Your Hooks

A hook generator AI gives you options. You still have to pick and test them. Here's the Hook Lab approach:

1. **Start with positioning, not wording.** Say in one line who the video is for and why they'll stop scrolling. If a hook doesn't serve that line, cut it.
2. **Pick one hook from each of three types.** For example, contrarian, callout, and result. Different types pull different viewers, so testing similar hooks teaches you little.
3. **Say it out loud and time it.** If the spoken line runs past about three seconds, shorten it. Twelve words is a good ceiling.
4. **Make the on-screen text work alone.** Plenty of people watch muted. The overlay should land the hook without audio, in a few words you can read at a glance.
5. **Deliver on the hook within the next few seconds.** A curiosity hook that never pays off trains viewers to scroll past you next time.
6. **Change only the hook.** Use the same script, length, and posting window, and swap just the first three seconds. Otherwise you won't know what caused the difference.
7. **Read your own retention graph.** Compare how many viewers stay past the opening on each version in your platform analytics. Keep the winning hook type and build the next batch around it.
8. **Use real numbers only.** Result hooks work because they're specific. If you don't have the figure yet, use a different hook type rather than inventing one.

## FAQ

**What is a hook generator AI?**
It's a tool that turns a topic, product, or trend into opening lines for short-form video. A good one gives you the spoken line, the on-screen text, and a mix of hook types so you can test. Hook Lab also writes the full script and caption around the hook you pick.

**Can I post AI-generated hooks as-is?**
Treat them as strong drafts. Swap in your real results wherever you see `[ADD: your number]`, adjust the wording to sound like you, and make sure the video delivers what the hook promises.

**How many hooks should I test per video?**
Start with two or three hooks of different types on the same script. Small batches with one variable are easier to read than many changes at once.

**Do the same hooks work on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts?**
The first-three-second structure carries across all three. Pacing, caption length, and on-screen text placement can differ by platform, so tell the generator which one you're filming for. Hook Lab defaults to TikTok at 30 seconds if you don't specify.
